done_when: On GitHub Actions (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true), forge test prints each line of the test command's output to the job log as it arrives, so a cancelled job still shows how far the tests got; outside GitHub Actions the output stays as it is now.

known.title: Gate: test live output before the test command exits
Follow-up: expose pytest's unfinished test-start output

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a GitHub Actions test command prints progress and then hangs until the job is cancelled. The named test calls `repo.forge`, which uses `subprocess.run` and returns only after Forge exits (`tests/conftest.py:319-326`). Removing `flush=True` or printing all output only after the command exits would still pass, while the cancelled job would again have no progress. The assertion also checks only the first marker, so dropped intermediate lines go undetected. The coordinator's marker-and-tail ruling did not address this timing gap. Extend the command-level test to observe the output while the test command is still running.
findings.title: Gate: test live output before the test command exits

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - a Python client runs `pytest -v` and a test hangs. The [pytest terminal reporter](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9.0.2/src/_pytest/terminal.py) flushes the test name before running it without a terminating newline. `test_output` holds that text until a newline or EOF (`src/forge/fasttest.py:594-600`), so the changed print path never exposes the hanging test's name before cancellation. This is additional evidence the coordinator's complete-line ruling did not weigh.
Adds work: surface unfinished progress as a job-log line; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Follow-up: expose pytest's unfinished test-start output

stop.reason: Round 1 finding goes back to the worker: prove output appears while the test command still runs

why: In a client's GitHub Actions tests job, forge test writes the test command's output only to a log file inside .git and prints the last 30 lines when the command ends. A job that hits the 60-minute limit is cancelled and shows no test output at all, so nobody can see which test was slow or hung.
